WHAT CHANGED

Lens information is not a calibration.

The original run did define a camera. It used one shared SIMPLE_RADIAL model: one focal length, a centered principal point and one radial distortion coefficient. With no focal metadata in the extracted PNGs, the initial guess was 1,152 px; COLMAP refined it to about 690.28 px, with k = 0.01973. The principal point stayed at (270, 480).

The new variant uses OPENCV: fx, fy, cx, cy, k1, k2, p1, p2. The nominal 26 mm-equivalent lens starts fx = fy at 693.33 px using the approximation 960 × 26 / 36. This assumes a full-frame-width equivalence; video crop and stabilization can change the effective value. It is an initial guess, not measured calibration. Focal lengths and distortion are refined; the principal point remains centered as in the baseline.

The metadata confirms the lens and aperture, but contains no calibrated intrinsic matrix or distortion coefficients. Aperture, shutter speed, ISO and white balance are capture settings, not COLMAP geometric calibration parameters. The phone's video crop, autofocus and stabilization can limit any single shared camera model.

The baseline is not inherently the wrong model. OPENCV offers more flexibility and can also overfit. This experiment changes both model complexity and focal initialization; it is not a pure single-variable test or a promise of improvement.

Reproducible setup

Exactly the original 500 PNGs at 540 × 960, linked locally without new resampling. CUDA-extracted SIFT features and raw matches are reused; geometric verification is repeated with the new intrinsics. Fresh incremental mapping and bundle adjustment run on CPU. Dense undistortion, CUDA depth estimation and CPU fusion follow after the active experiment queue releases the GPU.

Other matching pairs, mapping thresholds, camera sharing, principal-point policy and post-BA filtering remain at the baseline settings. The CPU mapping uses six threads so it can coexist with the ongoing GPU depth job. Full local outputs: experiments_local/iphone13pro_4x/colmap/4x/.

The 1,000-frame experiment now displays all sparse points in each component, including in the software renderer. Dense clouds remain sampled for browser display; complete PLYs stay local.
